body.p: Claims 1-10 were previously canceled. Claims 11-30 are currently pending. Claims 11, 14, 18, 19, 20, 29, and 30 are currently amended.
Claims 11-16, 18-23, and 25-30 are rejected as being unpatentable over Chahine et al. (US 2017/0056644) in view of Chen et al. (US 2010/0041975).
1. Chen does not teach or suggest "sense the generated signal from the at least one textile- based ECG generator electrode via the one or more textile-based ECG receiver electrode" as
recited by amended claims 11 and 29.

The present claims require a textile-based ECG electrode pairing having a textile-based ECG generator electrode that generates the generated signal, and a textile-based ECG receiver electrode that senses the generated signal.

Chen, paragraph [0046], describes: an "automatic selection process involves two steps in determining which electrodes to select to generate physiological data. First, the system searches electrode connections until it determines that a patient has come into contact with selected electrodes. Then, the processability and/or quality of the signal acquired is accessed."

The foregoing paragraph of Chen, describes a process of selecting sensing electrodes based on patient "physiological data." As such, Chen does not describe generating the generated signal, transmitting the generated signal through the at least one textile-based ECG generator electrode, and sensing the generated signal from the at least one textile-based ECG generator electrode via the one or more at least one textile-based ECG receiver electrode.
At least for this reason, claims 11 and 29 are considered to be patentable over the cited art.
2. Chen does not teach or suggest "based on sensing the generated signal... deselect the at least
one determined textile-based ECG electrode from the electrode pairing, and select another
textile-based ECG electrode pairing, repeat said generate and said sense of the generated
signal using the another textile-based ECG electrode pairing" as recited by amended claims

Claim 11 as amended requires certain steps in response to sensing the generated signal. In particular, deselecting the ECG electrode pairing, selecting another ECG electrode pairing, and repeating the process of generating and sensing the generated signal using the another electrode pairing. As discussed above, Chen does not have a generator electrode, and therefore, fails to teach the claimed ECG electrode pairing.

Furthermore, even if Chen is understood to have taught or suggested the claimed textile- based ECG generator electrode, there is no teaching or suggestion of: based on sensing the generated signal via the at least one textile-based ECG receiver electrode, determining that the at least one textile-based ECG generator electrode and/or the at least one textile-based receiver electrode of the textile-based ECG electrode pairing (i) is at least partially out of contact with the skin of the user and/or (ii) causes the generated signal that is transmitted through the at least one of the textile-based ECG generator electrode to be of unacceptable signal quality,
At least for this reason, claims 11 and 29 are considered to be patentable over the cited art.
